sources.title: Digital Tokyo Bay 1 TMK: HND12 new-build early-notification briefing, 6–7 August 2026
sources.publisher: Digital Tokyo Bay 1 TMK; USI Engineering; Kume Sekkei
sources.attribution: Digital Tokyo Bay 1 TMK; USI Engineering; Kume Sekkei
sources.summary: The developer’s 26-page neighbourhood briefing proposes HND12 at Toyosu 5-chome lots 2-15 and 2-63. It identifies Digital Tokyo Bay 1 TMK as building client, USI Engineering as project coordinator and Kume Sekkei as designer. The plans specify a 6,689.30 m2 site, approximately 4,500 m2 building area and 24,000 m2 gross floor area, six storeys, steel with some steel-reinforced concrete, and steel-pipe pile foundations. Construction was forecast for January 2027–August 2029, with preparation planned from November 2026 and staged operations from August 2029 onward while fit-out continues. Page 26 names MC Digital Realty as the intended operations manager and says it also promotes the project. The new-build contractor was undecided. Existing-building demolition appears separately with a planned January–December 2026 period; this does not establish an exact-day data-centre physical-work observation. Pages 17 and 18 explicitly give residential address Toyosu 5-4-9 and height 61.1 m.
sources.date_semantics: The cover explicitly dates these distributed briefing materials 6 and 7 August 2026. The developer’s accompanying page confirms both meetings took place and calls this their distributed material. The first distribution date, 6 August, is the publication/announcement date selected, not an inferred physical-work date. The file’s July 29 creation metadata is preparation, and Drive’s September 14 upload/modified dates are not announcement dates. The September 18 website opening is also kept separate.
sources.hosting_page: https://sites.google.com/view/toyosu-dc/説明動画配布資料/データセンター計画早期周知
sources.capture_note: Original 7,782,052-byte PDF fetched through Google Drive connector from the developer-linked file, then saved and hashed. Cover and pages 2, 4, 8, 26 rendered and visually reviewed; complete PDF text extracted for review. Google Drive metadata reports created 14 September 2026 11:32:00.022 UTC and modified 11:33:11.125 UTC; those upload timestamps are not used as document publication. No document imagery, full text, business contact details or raw file is redistributed. Copyright retained; Atlas uses compact factual paraphrases.

sources.summary: The EIA explicitly places the existing 220kV user substation within the northwest part of CIDC’s Ulanqab zero-carbon computing campus in the Bayin industrial area of Chahar High-Tech Zone. It gives the substation centre as E113°18′49.063″, N40°59′30.001″. Figure2 outlines the named campus in blue and the substation inside it in orange. The substation supplies the campus; this marker does not identify an individual data hall or the separate wind/solar step-up station about13km east. The EIA gives no explicit geodetic datum for the centre; the unshifted location was corroborated against georeferenced WGS84 imagery.
